There were factions which intended to nominate their own candidate for president of the Municipal Board, and then we asked the leadership to attend because we had ten boards, and we were all represented in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo, and each representative presented their problems an opinions. And President Karadzic was there, together with Krajisnik and other officials, and they suggested that we should find a peaceful and democratic solution. The majority of boards were in favour of appointing Mr. Brica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, the point was simply that if -- if you or other boards wanted the attention of the Bosnian Serb leadership at the republic level, you were able to request that and, in this instance, they appeared?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then on the 5th of May, 1992, you became the vice-president of the Executive Board of Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that would be the SDS Board, just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: On that Executive Board, not all the members of the SDS participated. There was one member of the board who was, let's say, a member of the socialist party, so you can't call it exactly the Executive Board of the SDS. It was established at the initiative of the Crisis Staff but not all of the members were from the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But the Executive Board that you were part of for Novo Sarajevo was the executive function or acted as the executive function for the Crisis Staff of Novo Sarajevo. Is that an accurate depiction?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So the Crisis Staff would make a decision. The Executive Board would implement those decisions.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No. The Crisis Staff initiated the establishment of the Executive Board, which was supposed to take over all the jobs that remained on the table after the previous board remained on the other side of the Miljacka river. The Crisis Staff did not interfere in -- in the business of the Executive Board because the Executive Board was doing its job quite well. There was no need for the Crisis Staff to meddle.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could be shown 65 ter 03290. We could start on page one for both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I see the B/C/S version is up on the screen. If you take a look at the upper left-hand corner, you would agree that this is a document coming from the Serbian municipality of Novo Sarajevo Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree this was dated 5 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if you will look to the last section of what's numbered as number -- well, number 1, would you agree that it reads: "The Crisis Staff has performed the function of Municipal Assembly in war conditions."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Up to a point, yes. Because not all the deputies were on our territory. So somebody had to take over the competencies of the Municipal Assembly until we established our own municipal me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And would you look at number 2 and agree that it reads -- actually if you'd listen: "An Executive Board was formed as an executive organ with the necessary secretariats that carried out the decisions made by the Crisis Staff." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Well, if we accept the above as true, that the functions of the Municipal Boards were taken over, then the following is also true, that the Executive Board implemented the decisions of the Crisis Staff and that was so until July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps I should have done this earlier but you would agree that this is a report on activities to the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I was not there, but I agree that it's true of most reports. I was not present for this one, but I believe that was the governing principle of our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You would agree that this document, in a simple read of its heading, was a report of activities to the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could have this document MFI'd, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not -- you're not seeking admission?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I will seek admission at this time, Your Honour. I will be coming back to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But then could we already see whether it can be admitted. You can still revisit the document. No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03290 receives number P6524, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Radan, going back to your chronology, on the 12th of July, 1992, you were elected president of the Executive Board of Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that members of the republic level of the Bosnian Serb leadership were present at this election?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, they were present. And I'm proud of that Assembly because it displayed a high degree of democracy. At the beginning there were three candidates, then two, and then one was chosen by a majority vote, by overwhelming majority. 24 out of 25 voted for him and one abstained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the simple question was whether the Bosnian Serb leadership was present. You apparently felt the need to explain how democratic it was. That was not part of the question. It's not disputed at this moment. So, therefore, there is no need to explain that. So would you please focus your answer on what has been asked. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In a very specific question you would agree that Dr. Nikola Koljevic was present?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And Petko Cancar?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: And Petko Cancar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that the presence of these individuals lent an importance to the election of new municipal leadership in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I think it did. It did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And in fact, in this capacity as president of this Executive Board, you enjoyed the ability to communicate, if needed, with the republic-level Bosnian Serb leadership?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. If needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And this is the position that you held until the 12th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And while in this position, you received information about what was happening on the ground from various municipal channels.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that you also received information from military organs in the area.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: At least once a week, we held meetings where the army, both police forces and civilian authorities, were present, and even outside of these meetings we were in touch.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that you had the full support of those organs for the work of the board.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: For the work of the Executive Board, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, let's briefly shift direction to the geography and the locations within the municipality of Novo Sarajevo. You would agree that there were significant locations and organs for the Serbian cause within the boundaries of Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I don't know which organs you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, let's --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have 65 ter 30676 placed on the screen. And this is a map. We do have hard copies which could be distributed for the Chamber. I believe the Defence has these maps. And we can provide a hard copy for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, before we look at these locations and organs, please take a look at the -- this map which depicts Novo Sarajevo and take some time to orient yourself.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you see the thick, dark lines on the map?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you know what the dark lines depict?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Those dark lines represent boundaries from before the war, the boundaries of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at the area dominating this map, would you agree that that would be the pre-war Novo Sarajevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, that was Novo Sarajevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would direct your attention now to the upper third of the map, towards the urban area where the city is located. If you could focus your attention just to the Miljacka river within Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do you see two lines, one marked red and the other blue?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: The blue dotted line and the red dotted line, yes, I see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Do the red and blue lines at the river depict the confrontation lines that were established in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: One of the lines. But this is directly on the Miljacka river, facing the other side. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree this confrontation line remained stable throughout at least your experience in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: There were minor shifts, almost none.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, please follow the red and blue lines towards Dobrinja on the map.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps with some, as I believe you described it, minor shifts, does this also depict the confrontation lines that you were familiar with in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: For the most part, yes, those were the positions. The demarcation line, the line that was defended.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that they roughly track the lines of -- or the municipal boundary at that point?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Well, at this point it trails off, and the territory of Ilidza and Novo Sarajevo remains outside of the line of conflict, confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But for the places where the confrontation line is within Novo Sarajevo, you would agree from the river to Dobrinja it roughly tracks the municipal boundary?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, it was a natural boundary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Pulling back and looking more at the lower two-thirds of the map, would you agree that in -- this area of Novo Sarajevo was under the authority of Bosnian Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes. It was under the authority of the Bosnian Serb authorities, and it was a municipality with majority Serbian population without any fluctuation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And it's when we get closer to the urban area that Novo Sarajevo had more of a multi-ethnic mixture in the population?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Novo Sarajevo, you mean before the outbreak of the war? Yes. And even in our part, it was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, just to verify a couple of locations. Am I correct that the Jewish cemetery is located within Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: The Jewish cemetery on our side. But the real Jewish cemetery remained outside Novo Sarajevo. We kept, we held the boundary, but the cemetery itself remained outside of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning to the military structures, you would agree that the SRK Corps Command was located in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the Lukavica barracks were obviously within Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And in terms of police, there was a police academy located in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, it was at Vrace.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And while the police special forces were a mobile unit, you would agree that they were based in different parts of Novo Sarajevo for the first months of the war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: With all due respect, I cannot agree that during the first few months of the war they were absent. In the first month of the war, yes, and then they went to different locations. I don't know exactly where. In any case, they were not permanently based at the police academy or in Novo Sarajevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It looks like you're at cross purposes. You said they were based in different parts of Novo Sarajevo. The witness says he doesn't agree that they were absent.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, to address the question, did you mean that the police special forces were present in Novo Sarajevo at the first month of the war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I said the first month, not the first few months. For the first month, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And the confusion is the way that it came out in the transcript. It appears that the police special forces were absent from Novo Sarajevo. Is -- is it -- just to clarify this: Were the police special forces present and located in Novo Sarajevo in the first month of the war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: They were present and located there in the first month of the war, and then they went to different parts of the territory as needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 30676.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30676 receives number P6525, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I -- thank you. We can take this image off the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, let's now turn to your statement. In paragraph 7 of your evidence, you say that unlike Muslims and Croats, the Serbs were not preparing for war. I'd like to go over the kinds of things that would constitute preparing for war. Would you agree that acquiring weapons would constitute preparing for war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes. Acquiring weapons means preparing for war.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You would agree that providing training for units, training them for military action, would also constitute preparing for war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree on that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that secretly preparing to take over municipal government functions would also constitute preparing for war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes. For those who did that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd first like to address the issue of training for military action. This Chamber has heard evidence that in 1991 the JNA provided training and arms to irregular forces of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm referring to P439, paragraph 7 to 14 in a section titled: "Training of SDS members by the JNA." We do not need to go to that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, were you aware that in 1991, in Sarajevo, the JNA was training and arming SDS irregular forces?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I didn't know that. First of all, I was actively involved in the work of the SDS in December 1991, that is clear. So my age did not allow me be trained and I did not -- I didn't know about this either. That is one thing. Secondly, the Serbs did rely on the JNA and they relied on Yugoslavia until the very last moment, we had no need to train, and we had not lost hope that we'd remain in Yugoslavia. So what I said here means that others were training and organising themselves. I do not have that experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the simple question was whether you were aware that in Sarajevo JNA was training and arming SDS irregular forces. The simple answer is you didn't know. And why you didn't know, if Ms. Bibles is interested in that or why it would be logical or not logical to know it, she'll ask you for it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I'm looking at paragraph 7 of your statement, and you say: "Unlike the Muslims and Croats, the Serbs were not preparing for war." So you would agree that you have proffered an opinion that is beyond your -- the scope of your personal experience?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No, that is my personal view, or my concrete view, because I did see such cases in Sarajevo. That is to say, I have taken an oath here that I will speak the truth and nothing but the truth and that's what I'm doing right now. So I do not know about training of Serbs or members of the SDS, whereas this I saw personally, the Green Berets, how they were dressed and everything else, and also how they moved around Sarajevo. This happened at once and it was all within the scope of preparations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, let's take a look at the some of the other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the court usher could bring P352, page 296 in English and P304 in B/C/S to our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While this is coming up, Mr. Radan, are you aware that General Mladic kept a notebook in which he recorded events?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I assume in relation to his precision in terms of his activity that he kept a notebook. As for the official notebook --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that he certainly had a notebook.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we missed part of what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I take over. What was recorded is the following, that you said: "As for the official notebook," and there the record stops, and then it resumes when you said: "I assume that he certainly had a notebook." What did you say between -- after the words "as for the official notebook," what did you then tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between these two sentences, my official knowledge of having a notebook, I found out from here, The Hague, that that was disclosed. General Mladic's notebook. On one occasion, I was directly present where he chaired a meeting, provided information, and I assume that the notebook comes from that meeting too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we're now looking at the -- the notebook dated 11 May 1992. I direct your attention to several lines below the underlined name of Colonel Kovacevic, where it reads: "I have been the brains of the weapons distribution for ten months and so far 69.000 Serbs have been armed." Have I read that correctly? You're -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now bring the first page of P3030 to the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we'll be looking at a 20 March 1992 JNA report, describing conclusions and evaluation of the situation on the Bosnia-Herzegovina territory within the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Military District. Do you see the signature on the bottom right-hand side of the page?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: With all due respect for you and the Court, I see all of this written here, but I was not informed about this at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I had a completely different post -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, that was not the question. I asked if you saw a signature at the bottom left-hand page -- I'm sorry, the bottom right-hand side of the page. Do you see a signature?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel General Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And who was he on the 20th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Sarajevo -- what was it called? The 1st District, or whatever, the 1st Sarajevo District. There were districts then and he was commander for Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could now turn to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, it appears to me that approximately 30 per cent of the questions you are putting to the witness are so obvious. I mean, to ask who this is, it says: "Commander General Milutin Kukanjac." And the heading is: "Command of the 2nd Military District." Now, unless there's any reason to believe that this commander is commander of something else, then it's -- it's useless. And similar questions about many things before. So try to focus on what would be reasonably in dispute and there are a lot of things, I think, that are not in dispute such as whether Novo Sarajevo, whether the part was during the war under Serb control. I don't think that there is much dispute about that, but I'm looking at Mr. Lukic. Many questions are really either obvious or do not need explanation, unless it's important for the witness to know. What you apparently are doing at this moment to show the witness why he didn't have the information to make a statement on whether the Serbs were preparing for war. That apparently is the issue. Now, that -- that is clear. But then to know exactly where Mr. Kukanjac was not only in this document the commander but he really was, where the witness has partially no idea, doesn't make much sense. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a witness who has proffered some pretty broad opinions and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. I'm not blaming you for putting, but I -- the question who Mr. Kukanjac was triggered my observation and it was in addition to a lot of questions before which were of similar obvious character and certainly matters that you could have easily, I take it, agreed upon with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the proposition the witness has put forward is that the Serbs were not preparing for war and I assume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not have to further explain. I fully understand your position, and I hope you understand my comments as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. If we could turn to page 4 in both versions at this point.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if you could direct your attention to the section that begins with "second." Please follow while I review a portion of this section: "The Serbian leadership and the Serbian people are fully prepared to wage a war ..." So you would agree that the JNA perceived that in March of 1992, the Serbian people were, in fact, prepared for a war?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I don't know where this conclusion comes from but I see that there is some mention here of Alija Izetbegovic. I don't see what I could say now by way of comment. March 1992, whether the army was ready. The army was ready to stay in Yugoslavia. I know that until the month of May, and the well-known things that happened in Dobrovoljacka Street and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, would you agree that based on the reading of this document and those words, that the JNA believed the Serbian leadership was prepared for war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I do apologise. I cannot make comments on something that I cannot see properly. I don't see the heading, I don't see who wrote this. I don't see who signed it. Prepared for war. No one felt like war.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, the reason I showed you the first page of this document and had you look at the signature was so that you would know who authored this document; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: This is one of the variants. It's possible that this was in the period when the Cutileiro Plan was there. That was in the month of March, so looking at the date, I can only link that up to that period that one of the proposals was a confederation. That is to say that if something that had been agreed upon is not accepted, something that had been agreed upon in Portugal, then there is no other option but for everyone to dig their heels into their own land and -- well, I mean, Izetbegovic came back and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: -- and did away with all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are giving a political analysis of the situation. The only thing Ms. Bibles is doing is putting to you a document in which it is stated, and she has given the letterhead and the signature of the person that presented this report which expresses that the "Serbian leadership and the Serbian people are fully prepared to wage a war." You, as a matter of fact, you're not denying it. You say: Well, if the political developments failed to do, then what else could we do? That's not the question. The question was whether this document expresses that the Serbs were prepared for waging a war, if circumstances would require them to wage such a war. Do you agree that that's what the document says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I agree with Mr. President but that can also be placed into a different context. I am being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- no, no. You're not invited to provide context. You're here to answer questions. You've said: Serbians were, unlike Muslims and Croats, not preparing for war. Now that's your opinion. Ms. Bibles, the only thing she does is to show you a few documents which apparently give a different position as to either preparing or being prepared for war. That's the only thing. As simple as that. We've listened to your last answer. You may move on, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's turn now with respect to the preparation in the realm of the political and government organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Novo Sarajevo Crisis Staff formed in 1991?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't have such information. I know about 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could bring 65 ter 3634 to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I'd like you to look at this document and see if this enhances your knowledge about the Crisis Staff and when it may have been in existence. Mr. Radan, would you agree that these are minutes, or an extract from minutes, perhaps, of a Crisis Staff meeting for 23 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I can just state that I know most of these names. But I was not present at that meeting, so there's nothing else I can say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you agree that the names that you recognise were active SDS members at that time.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: For the most part. For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And looking at the top, you would agree that the Crisis Staff heard and discussed the materials received from the SDS Bosnia-Herzegovina Main Board?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see that that is written there, but I'm testifying about what I know. So I know about the Crisis Staff from 1992, that established the first Municipal Board, and none of these persons mentioned here were on that board.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, you see on the left-hand side of this document there are items listed, with numbers?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that there are names opposite that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I can see that. I can read that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at item number 9. Would you agree that the three individuals there are from the civilian protection, the police, and the TO?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I don't know how relevant my testimony is if I was not present there in the first place. I repeat once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- just whether it's relevant or not, leave that to the parties and to the Chamber. There are three names there. Do you know these names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said a moment ago that I know the names of most of these people, and I know quite a few of them in person, but I am not aware of the offices that they seem to have held that are listed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm not asking you that. I just asked you if you say, "I know most of these names," then I want to ensure whether you know these three names. Do you know Mr. Kovac, by name or personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he have a function in the civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Executive Board that I presided over, he was in charge of matters related to military records. That is to say that he kept military records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was he involved --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Secretary of National Defence specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was he involved in civilian protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that period, when I was there, no. Until December 1992, he was in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jovanovic, do you know that name, Milanko Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Milanko Jovanovic was in the police. He was wounded in the beginning of the war and he left the municipality of Novo Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask all these questions, when he left, whether he was wounded or not. I just asked you whether you know him. Apparently you do. And he was in the Ministry of Interior in the police. Momir Garic. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Momir Garic was commander of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know when to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you should stop once you've answered the question. Apparently you know him. Was he -- did he have a function in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Commander of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, we -- actually, I'd ask to tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3634 receives number P6526, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I'd simply refer the Trial Chamber to P3038, which was Variant A and B instructions, and direct attention to the Variant A items with respect to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: But I'll move on, Mr. Radan. Mr. Radan, you agree that there were a number of preparations taking part on behalf of the Serb cause in preparation for war that you were unaware of?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Possibly. Because I do not have complete information.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we've looked at a number of documents here that show that there were preparations going on with respect to arming, training, and preparing the political structures. Would you agree that if you'd been asked, that you would have taken part in these activities?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Well, if I could help in any sense, if I could help towards a peaceful resolution of the situation, I would have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, let's talk now about the functioning municipal organs in which you participated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Although I believe we may be at a break point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are, Ms. Bibles. We take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. And we'll resume at 25 minutes past 1.00. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I put on the record that Judge Fluegge is with us again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, you may continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I'd like to start by going back to something that you said while testifying this morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be -- this line begins at page 38, line 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, you said: "The most important thing would have been the image we wanted to create of ourselves and the way we wanted to be perceived by the other ethnic groups, i.e., Muslims and Croats." You would agree that the police could secretly adopt a different attitude about the other ethnic groups? You would agree that the police could secretly adopt a different attitude or perception.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I can't agree with any such assumptions. I can't agree, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see P6524, and I direct attention to page 3 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, when this comes on the screen, I'd like to you look down at point 6 on the page, which would be titled: "Treatment of Muslims and Croats."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: It appears that we need to go to -- oh, yes, to page ... there we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, in this Crisis Staff report to the Presidency, under number 6, "Treatment of Muslims and Croats," it reads: "Citizens of all nationalities assemble frequently, especially in Grbavica, and our public attitude is very correct, we appoint a head of every building who is responsible for the situation in his building and for all the information about the occupants. Secretly, the police apply the usual procedure to people who were engaged in military activities against us." Would you agree, then, that the police could secretly adopt a different procedure towards the other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Well, everything was possible in the war and things were not possible. There were incidents. I don't have any information about such police activities, but things happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I'd like to move on now to paragraph 13 or matters that you discussed in paragraph 13 of your statement. You said there were nine men who -- "whom we knew by name." You name one of the men, Batko. Could you please name the other eight individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just try to object. I think the gentleman said: "I know some of them by nickname." I don't think that he ever claimed that he knows the names. But I will check in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll check in the transcript. The other eight people, could you, to the extent you remember, give names or nicknames or another identification of those persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At first I know of Batko whose name was Veselin Vlahovic. Then Zoran Zoka Cepter. Those are all nicknames. Krompir, and then some other nicknames. Believe me, I didn't know their full names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, it says you knew them by name. Now that doesn't specify whether it's their names or nicknames. But, Mr. Lukic, at least that's what the statement says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now let's not make it -- let's not make it more complicated. Could you, to the best of your abilities, give names or nicknames of the other eight, and I think you've given us now two. No, Batko whose name was Veselin. And then -- well, I think that the identity of Batko is -- could be then Zoran. Zoran who?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I don't know. There was somebody called Zoka Cepter and then another Zoka. I don't know. There was someone called Krompir, or Potato. Later I learned that his family name was Dragicevic. The police had that information. I just asked the police to intervene ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you knew them by names and you now are telling us that you don't remember all the names and only a couple of them and then mainly nicknames, sometimes even the same nicknames for two different persons. Ms. Bibles, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, you would agree that if you don't know who they are, you don't know for sure that they aren't part of some unit?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I knew and I know that they were not members of a unit because they always walked around Grbavica looking idle, without any commitments or obligations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, therefore, a conclusion, Witness. Because if people se me walking in the street, they wouldn't say I'm a member of a Court, so that is two different things. You concluded that the way in which you observed them, that they didn't show themselves to be members of a unit. That's how I understand your testimony now. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Precisely, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So, you as the president of the Executive Board were obviously aware of these individuals. Would you agree that other republic-level members of the Bosnian Serb leadership were aware of the activities of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Possibly they did. But I didn't know that they knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, in terms of these individuals being present in Novo Sarajevo and committing crimes, wouldn't you agree that it's -- it's an important distinction if people who could have done something about them, in fact, didn't?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: The desired reaction did not take place immediately, and when there were requests for these people to be removed from the area, it wasn't done immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that begs the question as to who knew they were there and when.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see P353, page 308 in the English and 306 in the B/C/S, this might help us understand this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we're looking at another notebook of Ratko Mladic. And this page that we'll be looking at is dated 10 July 1992. The B/C/S version is now on your screen. At this time, would you agree that as of 10 July 1992, Ratko Mladic knew that Batko was terrorising Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I suppose he knew because we wanted them removed. That initiative came from us. And military representatives were members of the commission which worked on that. General Milosevic was one of them as well as Major --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: -- he was from the military police. So it is quite possible that the information reached General Mladic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. We can remove this from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You would agree that Mrs. Plavsic lived in Novo Sarajevo, I think, until September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Mrs. Plavsic lived in Grbavica until May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. You would agree that she lived there during the time that Batko was present and active.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I said that she lived there until May or, rather, the end of April, the beginning of May. She was already in Pale at that time. Her mother went shopping. She came to visit her mother. She came to the municipality. She went wherever she deemed necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mrs. Plavsic made many other significant members of the Bosnian Serb leadership aware of the crimes that Batko was committing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could see the first page of 65 ter 17389A. This is an excerpt of a book from Mrs. Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, you've previously seen Mrs. Plavsic's book with respect to Batko, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: A correction, a slight correction. This is not Mrs. Plavsic's book but Mr. Rajko Vasic's book. The book was actually authored by Rajko Vasic, but it's based on her memories. I'm -- I'm aware of the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's look to the first paragraph -- or the -- the paragraph that starts about two-thirds of the way down the page. It's written: "I dashed to Pale in order to attempt to prevent the activities of crazy Batko. I entered into one of the rooms in Kikinda where I found all the persons relevant for the resolution of this problem. Radovan, Momo, Justice Minister Momcilo Mandic, and Interior Minister Mico Stanisic was there. I didn't even mention my conversation with Ogata to them. Instead, I immediately moved on to the events in Grbavica. I expected them to be surprised, concerned, dumbfounded, but there was nothing of the kind. Momcilo Mandic smirked (this is the right word to describe his face at that moment) and said, Ah, Batko. The interior minister reacted in the same manner as if we were talking about an unruly child and his games. So they knew about the man and his 'activities.' They knew him very well and did not hide this. So, they were his protectors and he received orders from them, which Zoran Vitkovic mentioned." Mr. Radan, having reviewed this section regarding Mrs. Plavsic, you would agree that the republican-level Bosnian Serb leadership was aware of Batko's activities?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Let me tell you, as far as I can remember, that book was written in 2005. And the references made here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, let me stop you -- let me stop you there. Ms. Bibles, the witness said: I didn't know that Biljana Plavsic was aware. Now to put a book to him in which apparently the author, which may or may not be Biljana Plavsic, says that she was aware and describes the circumstance and then to say to the witness: Wouldn't you agree -- I mean, the book speaks for itself. Whether the witness who says -- who has no knowledge, to ask him to say: Look at the book and wouldn't you agree with, that's, of course, not what the witness is supposed to do, and that's also not what you're supposed to ask from a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, would you -- wouldn't you agree that something could have been done to stop the crimes committed by these nine men much earlier?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Well, I said it just a while ago. I said that things could have been done, but there were omissions, and things were not done as soon as they had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, would you agree for the possibility that Batko and his men acted with the complicity of the Bosnian Serb leadership at least through September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I wouldn't jump the gun. I would not have issued that order for their arrest myself, so I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I would now like to turn to an issue that you have described in your statement and that you discussed this morning regarding the 30th of September, 1992, expulsion of non-Serbs or departure of non-Serbs from the Grbavica area. You testified this morning at T32, line 16 through the next line, that this was essentially a spontaneous internal agreement among the parties who lived in the area by the river. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Not around the river but in the Jewish cemetery, Gornji Kovacici --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter missed the last two names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the areas abandoned by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the last two names you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Donji Kovacici and Vrbanja.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, would you agree that there is a -- there is evidence of a different interpretation as to why the non-Serbs left the area on the 30th of 1992 [sic]?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: This is what I know, but I allow that different things may have been noted. So let's see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You are familiar with the Assembly of the Republika Srpska? And I should preface that, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I apologise. There were various, many Assembly sessions that were held in 1992. I don't know which one you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Well, let's look at an Assembly session or notes written by Ratko Mladic about an Assembly session on 14th of September, 1992, and see if we agree that they -- the events in this Assembly session might have impacted the departure of the non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have P344, page 4 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While we're waiting this to come up I'll ask you if you know who a Dr. Mitar Miljanovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Dr. Mitar Miljanovic is a law professor in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, we're looking again at Ratko Mladic's notebook for the 14th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And perhaps we need to go to the next page. I'm sorry, page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you look while I read -- what's reflected in the Ratko Mladic's notes: "The population of Grbavica is 80 per cent non-Serbian; implement the principle of retorsion." Can you tell us what retorsion is?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that term. But I did not attend that session. Why do you want me to interpret things or be the judge of things that happened there and as a result things were noted. How do I do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing Ms. Bibles is asking you whether you know what retorsion is. Your answer is: I don't know. No one asks for any judgement from you. Please proceed, Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, going to your own opinion --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And we can take this from the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In your own opinion, when you evaluate all of the circumstances of September 1992, you would agree that it's possible that crimes and harassment against non-Serbs in Novo Sarajevo led them to escape the area?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: What I know is completely different when it comes to the cause of their departure from Grbavica. If you will allow me, that was a separation line --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, you have testified here at ICTY twice now. You've testified in this trial, but you've previously testified in the trial with Radovan Karadzic. Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree that you were asked about whether the crimes and harassment against non-Serbs led them to escape the area in that trial as well. You recall that line of questioning?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes. And I also remember my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Would you agree that your answer, at -- the transcript reference is 31126, lines 15 to 18, are -- is: "It is possible, though, that the reasons you mentioned did exist, that people were being subjected to harassment, that they were seeking a way to cross over in order to escape such situations." Does that refresh your memory as to your answer on this line of questioning?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Absolutely. I remember that. It may have been one of the causes, but the main reason was the conditions of living. They were close to the separation line, exposed to the conflicts between the two sides. Well, they - both the Serbs and the Muslims who lived close to that separation line - agreed that they should both cross over to avoid being hit by a bullet and losing their life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification. I thought earlier you said that they left because of an internal mutual agreement. Now I hear you saying they left because they were in a war zone. Which is which, between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a factual situation. They were in a war zone. But they did agree. No agreement was signed though. However, there was a gentlemen's agreement among neighbours that they should be allowed to cross over to the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, to -- to actually get at the heart of this 30 September 1992 issue, let's go back to your experience. On that date, the 30th of September, you went to work in the municipal building about 8.30 in the morning. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You heard people talking inside and outside the building about a group of non-Serbs who crossed the Vrbanja bridge into Sarajevo. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, that is accurate. Many people used to gather in front of the municipality building at the time, but there were even more on that occasion, and those were their comments. And I checked that information with some authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, Mr. Radan, at that point, you got in your car, you drove to Pale, and you consulted with Momo Krajisnik. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No. On the 2nd of October, I met with President Krajisnik. So that was not on that same day, but on the 2nd of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Okay. You were told that this -- at that -- at that time -- that's when I want to get clarity on, you were told at some point that this was a voluntary movement of people organised by the Muslims themselves. Where did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: You couldn't do anything voluntary on that line without a prior action by the other side. It was their initiative to cross over in agreement with their Serb neighbours, and they were escorted safely to the Vrbanja bridge on the 30th of the September, around 6.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan - if we could see 65 ter 3358, please - earlier in your direct testimony, you discussed a -- that SRNA, I believe, is a news agency affiliated with the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When this document comes up, I will direct you into paragraph 2 where we see a statement from SRNA about this event. And this reads: "This was not a case of ethnic cleansing of Grbavica from which the official authorities and bodies of the Serb republic distance themselves. This was a case of some groups arbitrarily trying, through expulsion of Muslim citizens, to pressurise the Muslim authorities ..." So to be clear, the news agency of the Republika Srpska is saying that Muslims were expelled -- expelled to pressure the Muslim government. The statement goes on to say that the facts have been established in contacts with municipal representatives. So, Mr. Radan, this would suggest that the RS government said they had met with Serb municipal authorities in Novo Sarajevo. Would that have been you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I met with them on the 30th of September, and I see the SRNA report of the 1st October. They usually report very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: So the information we're reading here came from you? That's -- that's what I'm trying to articulate here.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't make a statement to the SRNA agency. This information was collected from several persons. It was not reporting from the site.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, this morning, at page -- transcript page 34, lines 1 and 2, you said that no one said -- "no one said there was an expulsion." You would agree that, in fact, the Republika Srpska's news agency was, in fact, saying there was an expulsion? So you would agree that your perception of this being some sort of negotiated agreement is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I stand by what I've said a moment ago. I can say nothing more based on this report. This is a collection, a summary of various other reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender 65 ter 3358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3358 receives number P6527, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, let's turn now to the 15th of November, 1992, symposium that is described or discussed in -- in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have page 2 of P1967 on our screens. Or perhaps I could fast-forward through this.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you present at the 15 November 1992 symposium, Mr. Radan?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's go head and turn to page 4 in both versions, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You would agree that Ratko Mladic was also present for this symposium?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: At the initiative of General Mladic, this meeting, this consultation, was held.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And at this symposium, an introduction was given by General Galic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And General Galic starts his introduction by talking about those things that are going well. Things like the enemy has been overstretched. The opponents' morale has dropped. And he ends that paragraph by saying: "Conditions for active offensive operations have been created." You're following with me in the minutes?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you would agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where exactly do we find this --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Bibles? Because apart from the witness -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At the very top of the English page, Your Honour. The enemy has been overstretched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I didn't see is who was speaking. That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If everyone agrees on the previous page. I can look at the previous page myself and then find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan -- and perhaps I can clear it up. Mr. Radan, these are comments that were made by General Galic in the introduction? Is that a yes? I'm sorry ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And then General Galic - excuse me - turns in his introduction to flaws, and in those flaws he reads, he states: "Genocide on other nations ..." Were you present for -- for the description or the discussion of the flaws?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I was there the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In the symposium, there was considerable amount of evidence or discussion of unnecessary mistreatment and killing of members of other ethnicities, especially Muslims. This was discussed in the symposium. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, some people also said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And in terms of some of the -- who was committing these kinds of offences, there was a discussion of crimes that were going on in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo. It would be in your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 12 in English and 9 and then 10 in the B/C/S versions, I would direct your attention to the record made by Prijic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Who was Prijic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Mr. Milivoje Prijic was president of the Novo Sarajevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In terms of who was responsible for offences, you would agree that he cited to problems involving robberies and shootings by various soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And anyone at the symposium would have been advised and aware that crimes by soldiers in Novo Sarajevo was a problem.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Those problems were absent only from Novo Sarajevo, but not in the sense spoken about by Mr. Prijic. I did talk about such problems, but that they should be qualified in this way and that that was happening on that scope, I -- no, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Mr. Radan, I think we have an issue with respect to the use of the English word "absent." Is it your -- the transcript would reflect that you said that: "These problems were absent only from Novo Sarajevo ..." Did you -- let's see if I can make this clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: I made a mistake probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Let's turn now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we would know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They existed not only in Novo Sarajevo but further afield.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to page 26 in English and then 17, quickly followed by 18, in the B/C/S versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you there when General Mladic spoke at the end of the symposium and addressed many points that had been raised?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: I think I wasn't there till the very end because those 20 buses from Sarajevo had arrived in Lukavica, so I didn't listen to all of it. I didn't hear all of it, and I'm very sorry about that, but I cannot confirm exactly at what time I left this gathering with the permission of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But earlier you said that you were there all the time. Just a few minutes ago you told us that you were there all the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the most part, I was present, and then Colonel Zarkovic said the buses arrived and somebody was to go out and meet them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Were you present when General Mladic spoke at the end of the symposium?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO RADAN
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And you heard him respond to the observations that had been raised in the symposium and say: "People's blood compels us to avenge them." Can you tell us, in your mind, what this was responding to?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I believe on the B/C/S version, we may need to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The signature is that of Aleksa Krsmanovic, Colonel, not General Mladic. Oh no, sorry, I see he just kept the record. I can't comment on what the General said but I agree that he was completely right, and -- I'm sorry, but I cannot give you my impressions from that symposium in one or two sentences. The point of the whole meeting was to reduce the problems on the ground, that military authorities, police authorities, and civilian authorities say and present their problems and then the tasks be issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not invited to tell us what the overall gist of this event was but you were asked what the line "people's blood compels us to avenge them," what that was a response to, if you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably he was referring to what was going on on the front line and the conducts that ran counter to conventions in waging war. That's how I understand it. I cannot interpret the General's words, but that's what I think. By that time, there had been Muslim offensives and killings, et cetera. So the idea was not blood for blood but to act as soldiers and wage war properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, I'm looking at the clock. I don't know exactly where we stand in terms of time. I see that you have used a little bit over one and a half hours so half an hour remaining tomorrow, 27 minutes to be very precise.
